notes: api-drift 1.0.0 does what its README says. A single per-note pass reads sessions, notes and turns, which are the inputs the drift check needs. It makes one call per matching note that a session touched or cited, and it works only on notes matching **/API*.md, **/api/** and **/Endpoints*.md, as the README states. The prompt restricts output to empty-old `append` changes under a final `## Drift` section and requires citations as {session, ordinal}. It forbids editing documented text, skips drift the note already records, treats every UNTRUSTED block as data, and keeps commands, instructions and links that only tool output shows out of the notes. The reviewer persona rejects by default, checks quotes against the cited turns, rejects tool-output-only sources, plans, guesses and non-append changes, and keeps a strict one-object JSON reply. The template is a plain skeleton with a descriptive sentence and no agent instructions, commands, links or credential handling. The test fixture is marked synthetic and uses obviously sample content. It also checks that a non-matching note (Meeting notes) is filtered out of the prompt, and the expected entry's quote and date match the transcript. I found no hidden, encoded or misnamed content and no embedded instructions aimed at the reviewer or the dreaming model.
